test_title: SSC CGL 2023 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 26 Jul 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom/phrase that can substitute the given group of words.

The better you know someone the less you like him.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. Familiarity breeds contempt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"Familiarity breeds contempt"** means that the more you know someone and become familiar with their flaws and shortcomings, the less respect or admiration you have for them. (परिचय का अपमान करना)

 
 
• **Example:** After working closely with his idol for a year, he realized that familiarity breeds contempt.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e., Familiarity breeds contempt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Save for a rainy day** (मुसीबत के लिए बचाना): To save money or resources for a time when they will be needed.

 
 
• **Example:** She always saves for a rainy day to ensure she's prepared for any unexpected expenses.
 
 
 
• **Spill the beans** (राज़ खोल देना): To reveal secret information or a surprise.
 
 
• **Example:** Please don't spill the beans about the surprise party tonight.
 
 
 
• **The elephant in the room** (सभी को दिखते हुए भी अनदेखी की जाने वाली महत्वपूर्ण बात): An obvious problem or controversial issue that no one wants to talk about.
 
 
• **Example:** The budget cuts were the elephant in the room during the meeting, but no one addressed them.
